title: address maphew review on PR #3562 — --skip-labels JSON path doesn't actually skip labels
description:
PR https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/3562 (feat(list): add --skip-labels hydration toggle, branch release/be-l9q, OUR PR). Reviewer @maphew (2026-05-26 20:10Z) found a real blocker:

'bd list --skip-labels --json still appears to take the normal JSON output path in cmd/bd/list.go: it calls activeStore.GetLabelsForIssues(ctx, issueIDs), assigns issue.Labels = labelsMap[issue.ID], and then calls outputJSON(issuesWithCounts) unconditionally. The new skipLabelsIssueView helper is defined an[d unused on the JSON branch].'

So --skip-labels works for the text path but the JSON path is unchanged — fix: wire the JSON branch through skipLabelsIssueView (or otherwise skip GetLabelsForIssues + omit Labels when the flag is set). Verify with bd list --skip-labels --json. Then push to release/be-l9q to refresh the PR.

This is our contribution PR — updating it is in-lane. The deny-list I just added (gastownhall/beads off-limits for mpr) does NOT apply to direct contributor work like pushing fixes to our own PR.
close_reason: Fixed with comprehensive solution from CI Bot that also optimizes storage layer to skip labels JOIN

title: Daily standup — 2026-06-06
description:
# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.
notes:
## What was done (last ~24h)

- Mayor delivered settled policy (gm-wisp-de1ldw): beads PRs (gastownhall/beads) are upstream — we do NOT merge, NOT authorize GC_MPR_ALLOW_UNMAINTAINED=1. These are 'authored, awaiting upstream.' Per-session CLEAN checks stop now.
- PR #4028 (fork-detect contributor routing, be-wqt8) confirmed merged to main earlier.
- Recent commits landed on origin/main: docgen CGO-binary federation guard (be-3cse, f288253ad), planning-schema fork fix (#4290, 0da7f51f3).
- Stale PR audits processed by reviewer: be-lehc (PR #3662), be-l13z (PR #3618), be-z6qf (PR #3998) — all closed.

## What's in flight

- **bd-lfak Phase 3** (bd preflight --fix): all implementation + test beads closed. PRs #4022, #4053, #4054, #4055 authored and CLEAN/MERGEABLE. Policy now: track as 'authored, awaiting upstream' — no more per-session status checks.
- be-fe4y (submit test PR) remains open, blocked on #4054 upstream merge. Same status.
- Sentry/mol-witness wisps cycling normally.

## What's blocking

- PRs #4022/#4053/#4054/#4055: gastownhall/beads maintainers must merge. Per today's policy this is not a GC action item — we wait.
- be-fe4y: blocked on #4054 upstream merge (same).

## What's next

- Update bd-lfak plan to drop per-session CLEAN check language; mark 'authored, awaiting upstream.'
- Check for any new work (architect/designer handoffs).

## Questions for mayor (optional)

None — today's policy message settles the open questions.

Verdict: PREMISE OBSOLETE -- recommend CLOSE (no-longer-wanted) or REWORK. Exit (d): escalated to mayor (close/rework is a maintainer/product call, not this seat).

Verified vs fresh origin/main:
- Ours (author quad341). MERGEABLE, ALL CI green, purely additive (+144/-0: cmd/bd/main.go guard + cmd/bd/main_errors_test.go + release gate). No inline/review comments; only codecov bot (80% patch coverage -- not a blocker).
- PR adds checkMetadataBackendError(): if metadata.json declares backend != dolt (e.g. postgres), FatalError "This bd binary does not support the <backend> backend... Upgrade bd to a version that supports <backend>: curl install.sh | bash; brew upgrade beads".

Why the premise drifted:
- Postgres was a real backend effort (feat(postgres): bd init --backend=postgres, --pg-* flags, PG health/bench) that was SCRUBBED from the public codebase: be-bhrzia "scrub pgx/postgres from public beads codebase", committed 2026-05-16 22:21 UTC -- ~2.5h AFTER this PR was filed (2026-05-16 19:49 UTC). Same-day concurrent work; the PR landed on the wrong side of the scrub.
- Current public origin/main: NO postgres. init_postgres*/postgres_health.go gone, no pgx, `bd init` only supports --backend dolt. configfile.Backend is "Deprecated: always dolt"; GetBackend() unconditionally returns dolt; startup path does NOT read the raw .Backend field for behavior (PR's guard reads it; nothing else does).

Consequences on current main:
1) Guard remediation is UNFOLLOWABLE: it tells users to upgrade via public install.sh/brew to "a version that supports postgres", but the public binary is dolt-only -- no such public version exists. Misleading advice shipped to users.
2) The motivating symptom (stale pre-PG binary silently entering multi-GB/30-60s postgres fallback, be-y0sm9s/be-bx0tm7) likely NO LONGER reproduces: no postgres code path remains; backend=postgres is simply ignored (treated as dolt via GetBackend()).

Out-of-rig open question for mayor: there is a `no_dolt` build tag for a "PG-only bd binary" (be-mlavwq) -- postgres may survive behind a build tag / private repo. Even so, the PUBLIC channels the error names don't restore postgres, so the message is wrong for the public binary regardless. (Did not chase private-PG topology; not needed to decide this public PR.)

Recommendation to mayor: CLOSE PR #3998 as no-longer-wanted (premise obsolete). If a generic "unsupported/unknown backend -> clear error" guard is still wanted, REWORK the message into a removal/migration hint (not "upgrade for postgres support") -- an architecture/product call. Did NOT post on GitHub (city policy). Escalated via mail.

title: Harden generate-cli-docs.sh against CGO-binary federation doc drift
description:
## Root cause
generate-cli-docs.sh selects its bd binary as: $1, else $PROJECT_ROOT/bd, else builds CGO_ENABLED=0 -tags gms_pure_go. When a CGO-enabled ./bd is left in PROJECT_ROOT (e.g. from `make build` during a builder/deployer session), a no-arg call regenerates docs from it. A CGO bd exposes the CGO-only `bd federation` subcommands, so the regen writes federation subcommand pages into docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md, website/{docs,versioned_docs/version-*}/cli-reference/federation.md and website/static/llms-full.txt. CI's check-doc-flags builds CGO_ENABLED=0 (scripts/ci/pr-policy.sh build_docs_binary) whose bd emits NO federation subcommands -> doc-flags fails and cascades to Build Artifacts / PR Policy / CI Gate. Hit PRs #3710, #4055, #4153 simultaneously on 2026-06-06 (each fixed by regenerating with a pure-go binary).

## Fix spec
In scripts/generate-cli-docs.sh, make doc generation CI-consistent regardless of stray binaries. Recommended: after resolving $BD, probe it (`"$BD" federation --help`) and if it does NOT print the "Federation commands require CGO" stub (i.e. it is a CGO build that exposes subcommands), either (a) ignore it and build a fresh CGO_ENABLED=0 binary internally, or (b) abort with a clear message instructing to pass a CGO_ENABLED=0 build. Prefer (a) for robustness; keep the explicit-arg fast path only when the arg is already pure-go. Apply the same guard to the $PROJECT_ROOT/bd fallback. Add a one-line comment pointing at scripts/ci/pr-policy.sh build_docs_binary as the oracle.

## Out of scope
- Do NOT remove the CGO-only federation subcommands or change CGO build behavior.
- Do NOT touch check-doc-flags.sh / check-doc-freshness.sh / pr-policy.sh.
- Do NOT regenerate committed docs in this bead (that is per-PR work).

## Done-when
- [ ] Running generate-cli-docs.sh with a CGO ./bd present in PROJECT_ROOT no longer emits federation subcommand pages (matches CGO_ENABLED=0 output).
- [ ] LC_ALL=C ./scripts/generate-cli-docs.sh <pure-go bd> still produces zero churn on a clean main.
- [ ] check-doc-flags.sh + check-doc-freshness.sh pass after a regen on main.
- [ ] A short note in the script references the CGO_ENABLED=0 CI oracle.
close_reason: Implemented CGO guard in generate-cli-docs.sh. After resolving bd binary, probes 'bd federation --help'; if no pure-go stub, rebuilds CGO_ENABLED=0 binary internally. All done-when criteria met. PR #4312 (quad341:fix/be-3cse-cgo-docgen-guard → gastownhall/beads main).

# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).

title: Daily standup — 2026-06-03
description:
# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.
notes:
### What was done (last ~24h)

- **PR #4023 (reference-aware bd prune) fixed and green.** Investigator diagnosed the root cause (main's wholesale doc regen on 2026-06-03 dropped the newly-added `migrate-personal.md` page from the 1.0.5 versioned snapshot, killing doc-flags CI). Fix: regenerated via `generate-cli-docs.sh ./bd`, committed, pushed. All 51 CI checks now pass — PR is PASS (maphew review) + green; merge-ready (be-nzyb).
- **PR #4058 (--quiet flag wiring) escalated to mayor.** Investigator confirmed: still novel vs main, already approved in pack review, only step left is merge authority. Mayor has mail (be-g438).
- **PR #4059 (bd doctor --check=pollution docs) escalated to mayor.** Same situation — docs-only, CI green, pack-approved, no code fix needed. Mayor has mail (be-68h0).
- **PR #4300 merged** (proxied server list command, coffeegoddd). PR #4299 also merged (community tools website page).
- **Narrow-projection perf arc active on branch**: `SearchIssueSummaries` added (be-3ht), release gate PASS committed, `WispIDSetInTx` amortization landed, unit tests for `sortSummaries`/`useSummary` in (be-2kl). Rebased onto main's `WispIDSetInTx(ids)` API (be-el0). Not yet in a PR.

### What's in flight

- **Schema-skew detection family (be-4259)**: PRs #4266 (deterministic dep PKs), #4268 (silent-migration prevention gate), #4269 (parallel t.Setenv fix), #4270 (per-migration content hash + bd doctor skew detection) — all open, awaiting review/merge.
- **GitLab dependency sync** (#4294) — open, awaiting review.
- **Conflicting-deps fix** (#4286, six typed dep tables) — open, has one comment but no blocking review.
- **Other infra fixes in queue**: #4288 (skip empty dolt commit), #4284 (bound embedded dolt timeout), #4281 (dolt push hooks), #4290 (planning init fork fix), #4296 (dolt federation runtime dir discriminator), #4289 (index metadata fields).
- **Witness-patrol mol** (be-wpuv) cycling — substeps open for orphan reset, queue depth report, and next patrol iteration.

### What's blocking

- PRs #4023, #4058, #4059 are all merge-ready but need merge authority (operator/mayor/mpr). Investigator escalated #4058 and #4059 to mayor via mail; #4023 is also waiting.
- No code defects blocking any of the above — pure pipeline throughput.

### What's next

- Mayor action on #4058 and #4059 (two ours-authored PRs, both approved, safe to merge).
- Merge #4023 (reference-aware prune, green + PASS review).
- Review pass on #4286 (conflicting deps) — it has a comment that may need a response before it clears.

title: Fork auto-config creates ~/.beads-planning/.beads without initializing a Dolt DB; migrate-personal then fails
description:
Source: maphew review of PR #4023 (gastownhall/beads), finding 4 (P2). Filed by investigator while addressing that review; this part is OUT OF SCOPE for PR #4023 because the code lives on origin/main (merged via #4028), not in the PR diff.

## Bug
`autoConfigureForkContributor` (cmd/bd/init_contributor.go ~L295-315) creates ~/.beads-planning and ~/.beads-planning/.beads via os.MkdirAll + `git init`, but does NOT initialize a beads/Dolt database there. `bd migrate-personal` (cmd/bd/migrate_personal.go:92-95) only checks that the .beads directory exists, then opens the planning store directly via dolt.New (L118-126). A contributor who runs `bd init` in a fork and immediately runs `bd migrate-personal` hits an uninitialized planning store ("Dolt server unreachable" / failed to open planning store).

Secondary (same finding): idempotency in autoConfigureForkContributor checks only the DB config (store.GetConfig routing.contributor); a YAML-configured contributor setup could be missed.

## Suggested fix direction (needs a small design call)
Either (a) initialize the planning Dolt DB (schema) during fork auto-config, or (b) have migrate-personal initialize/validate the planning store on demand before opening it. Add a regression test: `bd init` on a fork then `bd migrate-personal` must not fail on an uninitialized planning store.

## Verification context
PR #4023 took main"'s init.go/init_contributor.go during rebase (commit a07145d8e), so autoConfigureForkContributor is main code. Confirmed the function still creates .beads without DB init at HEAD.
notes:
Implementation plan: Approach (a) — initialize planning Dolt schema during fork auto-config.

Changes:
1. cmd/bd/init_contributor.go: autoConfigureForkContributor now initializes the planning store via newDoltStoreFromConfig after creating ~/.beads-planning/.beads. Non-fatal for no-CGO/server-mode builds. Also extends idempotency check to cover YAML-configured contributor setups (secondary acceptance criterion 4).
2. cmd/bd/init_embedded_test.go: fork_auto_contributor sub-test gains assertion that planning embeddeddolt dir is created (proving schema init ran).
close_reason: Implemented approach (a): planning Dolt schema now initialized during fork auto-config. Regression test added to fork_auto_contributor. Both builds compile clean; doc-flags CI pass. Committed as 1d9c835a2.

title: Daily standup — 2026-05-31
description:
# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.

# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.

title: Decision: PR #3458 'benchmark-only' split is infeasible (won't compile) — pick direction
description:
DECISION NEEDED (mayor): PR #3458 — the maintainer's "benchmark-only split" is
infeasible as literally stated. Pick the direction. Investigator has a ready-to-post
upstream reply; NOT posting it autonomously (this PR has a flagged history of a bot
acting on fabricated data — see be-vd65). Original audit bead routed this as "(d)
escalate to mayor."

All facts below are from LIVE gh + a compiler artifact, not bead notes. The earlier
be-vd65 notes contained fabrications (retracted there) AND the "correction" note also
misread one comment; both are superseded by this.

================================================================================
VERIFIED STATUS (live, 2026-05-31)
================================================================================
PR #3458 https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/3458
 - OURS: author quad341 (Jim Wordelman) = gh-authenticated user. Cross-repo fork PR
   (quad341/beads:release/be-nu4.3-stack -> gastownhall/beads:main).
 - state OPEN, reviewDecision CHANGES_REQUESTED, mergeable MERGEABLE / UNSTABLE.
 - CI: red on exactly 2 MECHANICAL checks — "Check formatting" (gofmt on cmd/bd/list.go)
   and "Check doc flags freshness" (stale docs/llms-full.txt). Every test/lint/build/
   regression/upgrade-smoke PASSES.
 - Dependent open PR #3461 (be-nu4.4 result cache) is stacked on this one.

REVIEW TIMELINE (verified):
 - 2026-05-07 coffeegoddd CHANGES_REQUESTED: "too complicated... too many layers...
   start from the database layer (issueops)... mostly SQL queries without so many
   application code changes."  -> ARCHITECTURE concern.
 - 2026-05-08 WE addressed it (commits 33309b7d + dc9f9769): pushed narrow-projection
   into issueops, SQL-side sort (SortBy/SortReverse + BuildSummaryOrderBy), deleted the
   parallel Go-side formatters/sorters. Net -993/+154 on the refactor commit.
   => The 05-07 architecture concern is ADDRESSED. This part is NOT what's blocking.
 - 2026-05-17 coffeegoddd COMMENTED: "take just dolt_benchmark_test.go with no comments
   in this pr, then on a subsequent pr we can get the perf improvements and see the bench
   results on main versus on the fix pr."  -> SPLIT request.
 - 2026-05-17 WE replied offering to do exactly that split ("Want me to set those up?").
 - 2026-05-27 maphew (codex on behalf of matt wilkie, acting maintainer) RE-ENDORSED the
   split: "keep only internal/storage/dolt/dolt_benchmark_test.go in this PR, then move
   the narrow-projection/perf implementation into a follow-up PR." => This effectively
   ANSWERS our 05-17 question: yes, split. (The old be-vd65 note claiming maphew asked a
   "--json output" question is WRONG — there is no such comment on this PR.)
 - 2026-05-20 / 2026-05-29 WE only rebased; the split was OFFERED but NEVER EXECUTED.

So the live blocker = the SPLIT, wanted by two maintainers, which we never did.

================================================================================
THE BLOCKER: the literal split does NOT compile (PROVEN)
================================================================================
The PR's benchmark additions (BenchmarkSearchIssueSummaries_1K/10K/50K, via
benchmarkSearchIssueSummaries + seedForSummaryBench) call:
    store.SearchIssueSummaries(ctx, "", types.IssueFilter{})

`SearchIssueSummaries` is ABSENT from main — 0 occurrences of the bare string anywhere
in origin/main. It is INTRODUCED by THIS PR, defined only in files the split would drop:
    internal/storage/dolt/queries.go:36              (DoltStore)
    internal/storage/embeddeddolt/list_queries.go:35 (EmbeddedDoltStore)
    internal/storage/issueops/search_summary.go:78   (SearchIssueSummariesInTx)
    internal/telemetry/storage.go:207                (InstrumentedStorage wrapper)

Compiler artifact (/tmp/be-vd65/compile-proof.txt). Reproduce:
    git worktree add --detach /tmp/wt origin/main
    cd /tmp/wt
    git checkout ccfe9500 -- internal/storage/dolt/dolt_benchmark_test.go
    CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go -c -o /dev/null ./internal/storage/dolt/
  =>
    internal/storage/dolt/dolt_benchmark_test.go:1982:22: store.SearchIssueSummaries
    undefined (type *DoltStore has no field or method SearchIssueSummaries)

So "take JUST dolt_benchmark_test.go" yields a non-compiling PR. The maintainer's
premise — that there is an existing method on main to benchmark — does not hold for
this optimization: the method IS the feature.

================================================================================
SECOND FACT THE MAINTAINER LACKS: a main baseline already exists
================================================================================
main's internal/storage/dolt/dolt_benchmark_test.go ALREADY has:
    BenchmarkSearchIssues       (line 423)
    BenchmarkSearchWithFilter   (line 455)
covering the existing full-row `bd list` backing path. So a "baseline on main" for the
list path effectively already exists. The new BenchmarkSearchIssueSummaries_* measures
the NEW narrow method and can only live alongside its implementation.

================================================================================
OPTIONS
================================================================================
A. RE-ENGAGE THE MAINTAINER (recommended). Reply on our PR with the two facts above
   (split won't compile; main already benchmarks the full-row path) and let coffeegoddd/
   maphew re-decide. Concretely offer: keep the perf PR as one PR (it already contains
   both the method and its benchmark) and compare main's BenchmarkSearchIssues (baseline)
   vs the PR's BenchmarkSearchIssueSummaries (narrow). If they still want a separate
   benchmark-first PR, the minimal compilable unit is "benchmark + the SearchIssueSummaries
   method" — benchmark-alone is not achievable. Draft reply below; needs go-ahead to post.
B. BUILDER-EXECUTE A SPECIFIC SPLIT. If we instead decide the cut line ourselves (e.g.
   land a minimal SearchIssueSummaries + benchmark on main first, optimize in a follow-up,
   then rebase #3461), hand a builder a precise spec. This overrides the maintainer's
   literal "just the benchmark" instruction, so it should be paired with an explanatory
   PR comment so it doesn't read as ignoring them.
C. SHELVE/CLOSE the be-nu4.x perf stack if it's no longer a priority (also reassess #3461).

CI note: the 2 red checks (formatting on cmd/bd/list.go; doc-flags/llms-full.txt) are
byproducts of the cmd/bd changes. If we split them out they clear automatically; if we
keep the PR whole they're a ~2-minute mechanical fix. Either way, not the blocker — do
NOT burn a force-push on them until the direction above is chosen.

================================================================================
DRAFT UPSTREAM REPLY (for approval — NOT posted)
================================================================================
@coffeegoddd @maphew — picking this back up, thanks for the patience.

Two things I hit trying to carve out the benchmark-only PR you suggested:

1. A benchmark-only PR won't compile on its own. The new benchmarks
   (`BenchmarkSearchIssueSummaries_*`) call `store.SearchIssueSummaries(...)`, which this
   PR introduces — it doesn't exist on `main` yet. So "just `dolt_benchmark_test.go`"
   has no method to call until the implementation lands. The smallest self-contained
   unit would be "benchmark + the `SearchIssueSummaries` method," not the benchmark alone.

2. `main` already benchmarks the existing list path (`BenchmarkSearchIssues`,
   `BenchmarkSearchWithFilter`), so there's already a baseline to compare against. The
   new benchmark measures the narrow-projection method specifically.

Given that, would you prefer: (a) keep this as one PR — you can read the before/after as
main's `BenchmarkSearchIssues` vs this PR's `BenchmarkSearchIssueSummaries`; or (b) a
first PR that lands the `SearchIssueSummaries` method + its benchmark (compiles, gives a
same-method baseline), with the cmd/bd wiring + narrow-projection refactor in the
follow-up? Happy to shape it whichever way reads cleanest for you.
================================================================================
notes: DECISION 2026-06-05: HOLD. The June 3 re-review comment (quad341, PR #3458) already reframes the split question: PR #4032 landed baseline benchmarks on main; #3458 is the subsequent perf PR. Material context is already in the thread. Mayor guidance (gm-wisp-w1oopi): lean deferential, exception only if draft aids coffeegoddd's re-review — judgment call is that it does NOT add to what's already posted. Wait for coffeegoddd to respond.

title: Fix: force LC_ALL=C in generate-llms-full.sh to stop recurring doc-flags drift
description:
## Root cause
scripts/generate-llms-full.sh:142 expands `"$DOCS_DIR/$dir"/*.md` globs whose
ordering is LC_COLLATE-dependent. CI's "Check doc flags freshness" runs under the
C locale (byte collation), which orders e.g. cli-reference/init-safety.md BEFORE
init.md ('-' 0x2D < '.' 0x2E). A developer/agent on a UTF-8 locale generates the
opposite order, so the committed website/static/llms-full.txt drifts from what CI
regenerates and the check fails. doc-flags runs on pull_request only (not
push-to-main), so main's committed copy is never validated and silently drifts;
the failure surfaces whenever a PR merges main. Recurred on PRs
#3908 / #3985 / #4157 / #4160 / #4212. The script header claims determinism but
never pins the locale.

## Reproducing repro (no Go build needed)
On a UTF-8 locale (e.g. en_US.UTF-8):
  ./scripts/generate-llms-full.sh                    # writes UTF-8-ordered file
  LC_ALL=C ./scripts/generate-llms-full.sh --check   # FAIL: ordering differs
Confirm init.md vs init-safety.md order flips between the two runs:
  grep -n 'document path="docs/cli-reference/init' website/static/llms-full.txt

## Fix spec
1. In scripts/generate-llms-full.sh, add `export LC_ALL=C` immediately AFTER the
   existing `set -euo pipefail` line (currently line 7). This pins glob/sort
   collation to byte order for every invocation, matching CI exactly.
2. Regenerate once and commit the canonical C-ordered file:
   `LC_ALL=C ./scripts/generate-llms-full.sh` (likely a no-op now that PR #4212
   landed a C-ordered llms-full.txt on main; include any diff if main drifted
   again by build time).
3. Do NOT fix this only at call sites — pin it inside the script so it is
   locale-proof for humans and agents alike.

## Out of scope
- Making doc-flags also run on push-to-main (separate CI-policy decision; raise
  with the architect if warranted, but don't implement here).
- Touching check-doc-freshness.sh or generate-cli-docs.sh logic.
- Regenerating versioned_docs snapshots.

## Done-when
- [ ] ./scripts/generate-llms-full.sh produces byte-identical output to
      LC_ALL=C ./scripts/generate-llms-full.sh regardless of caller locale.
- [ ] ./scripts/generate-llms-full.sh --check passes under both default locale and LC_ALL=C.
- [ ] CI "Check doc flags freshness" passes on a PR that merges current main.
notes: adr_check: skipped — actual CLI not installed. Proceeding with implementation.
close_reason: Added export LC_ALL=C after set -euo pipefail in scripts/generate-llms-full.sh. Both ./scripts/generate-llms-full.sh --check and LC_ALL=C ./scripts/generate-llms-full.sh --check pass. llms-full.txt was already C-ordered (no-op regen). Committed as 8e07ad962.

design:
# Design: `NoPush` Field in `RenderOpts` — Template UX and Rendered Output

**Bead:** be-xj7  
**Author:** beads/designer  
**Architecture ref:** be-j28 (FR-3, FR-4, NFR-3, NFR-4)

---

## Context

`bd init` and `bd setup <agent>` render a "Beads Integration" section into
`AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`. The current template always includes `bd dolt push`
in the Session Completion checklist. On no-push rigs, this step fails and
blocks agent completion. The fix is to strip `bd dolt push` from the rendered
output when `NoPush=true`.

Primary readers of the rendered template are AI agents. Secondary readers are
human operators reviewing the file.

---

## Design decisions

### Q1 — Omission vs. commented-out line

**Decision: pure omission** (as specified by architect).

Option A (accepted): strip the line, nothing in its place.
Option B (rejected): leave a comment — `# bd dolt push  # Skipped: no-push: true`.

Rationale for omission:
- AI agents execute code blocks literally. A commented-out line creates ambiguity:
  "should I un-comment this?" Some agents will attempt to remove the comment and run
  the command anyway, defeating the entire feature.
- The `bd prime` command (unchanged by this PR) already explains session-close
  protocol correctly for no-push rigs. That is the right place for explanatory context.
- Pure omission is semantically unambiguous: the step does not exist on this rig.
- The existing `HasRemote=false` path already uses pure omission for the same line —
  consistency with the established pattern. ✓

---

### Q2 — Impact on "PUSH TO REMOTE" heading

**Decision: heading stays as-is, no wording change needed.**

The Session Completion heading reads:
```
**PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
```
And the critical rule says:
```
- Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds
```

Both remain accurate on no-push rigs because `git push` still runs. Only `bd dolt push`
is removed. The heading's intent is to ensure the git push happens — it is not specific
to Dolt sync. No heading or critical-rule wording changes are needed.

---

### Q3 — Auto-Sync section (full profile)

**Decision: strip the remote-sync bullet, preserve the auto-commit bullet.**

Current Auto-Sync section (full profile):
```
bd automatically syncs via Dolt:
- Each write auto-commits to Dolt history
- Use `bd dolt push`/`bd dolt pull` for remote sync
- No manual export/import needed!
```

After stripping (NoPush=true):
```
bd automatically syncs via Dolt:
- Each write auto-commits to Dolt history
- No manual export/import needed!
```

Rationale:
- The auto-commit bullet is still true on no-push rigs. ✓
- The remote-sync bullet is false/irrelevant on no-push rigs. Stripping it prevents
  agents from attempting `bd dolt push/pull`.
- "No manual export/import needed!" remains accurate — auto-commit still works. ✓
- The section header "Auto-Sync" remains accurate — commits still auto-sync to
  local Dolt history; they just don't reach a remote.

---

### Q4 — `NoPush=true` + `HasRemote=true` edge case

**Decision: NoPush wins — strip the push line regardless of `HasRemote`.**

An operator who sets `no-push: true` has made an intentional policy decision. Even
if a remote is technically configured, the rig should not push. The template must
honor the declared policy, not the inferred capability.

The condition `if !opts.HasRemote || opts.NoPush` correctly captures this:
- Push stripped when no remote configured (existing behavior).
- Push stripped when `no-push: true`, regardless of remote (new behavior).

No UX change needed — the existing `stripDoltPushReferences` function is called in
both cases. The rendered output looks identical whether triggered by `HasRemote=false`
or `NoPush=true`.

---

### Q5 — `bd doctor` freshness detection

**Decision: rely on existing hash-based detection, no additional plumbing.**

The template hash changes whenever `NoPush` changes (because the rendered body changes).
Rigs that already have a rendered AGENTS.md will see a freshness mismatch on the next
`bd doctor --check=agents` run. This correctly prompts agents to re-run `bd init`.

No new UX surfaces needed. The existing `bd doctor` staleness message is sufficient.

---

## Template before/after (minimal profile)

### Before (NoPush=false — existing behavior)

```
## Session Completion

**When ending a work session**, you MUST complete ALL steps below. Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds.

**MANDATORY WORKFLOW:**

1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create issues for anything that needs follow-up
2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
   ```bash
   git pull --rebase
   bd dolt push
   git push
   git status  # MUST show "up to date with origin"
   ```
5. **Clean up** - Clear stashes, prune remote branches
6. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
7. **Hand off** - Provide context for next session
```

### After (NoPush=true)

```
## Session Completion

**When ending a work session**, you MUST complete ALL steps below. Work is NOT complete until `git push` succeeds.

**MANDATORY WORKFLOW:**

1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create issues for anything that needs follow-up
2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
4. **PUSH TO REMOTE** - This is MANDATORY:
   ```bash
   git pull --rebase
   git push
   git status  # MUST show "up to date with origin"
   ```
5. **Clean up** - Clear stashes, prune remote branches
6. **Verify** - All changes committed AND pushed
7. **Hand off** - Provide context for next session
```

**Diff:** one line removed (`   bd dolt push`). All surrounding content is preserved
and remains semantically accurate.

---

## Accessibility audit

1. **Agent code-block execution:** Agents execute code blocks in order. After stripping,
   the block contains only valid, applicable commands. No phantom step, no commented-out
   step, no ambiguous no-op. ✓
2. **Human readability:** The stripped template reads naturally. "PUSH TO REMOTE" is
   followed by `git push` — the expected action. No cognitive gap. ✓
3. **Markdown validity:** Stripping a single indented line from a code block leaves
   valid Markdown. The triple-backtick block is intact. ✓
4. **`bd doctor` signal:** Hash change on `NoPush` flip → clear staleness signal. ✓

---

## Implementation verification checklist (for builder)

- [ ] `stripDoltPushReferences` matches exactly three-space-indented `   bd dolt push\n`
      (not tab-indented, not two/four spaces). A mismatch silently fails.
- [ ] All 7 callsites propagate `NoPush` from the config read — especially
      `init_proxied_server.go` (the sole external callsite with least test coverage).
- [ ] Unit test: `stripDoltPushReferences("   bd dolt push\n")` returns `""`.
- [ ] Integration test: `bd init` on a rig with `no-push: true` produces an AGENTS.md
      that does NOT contain `bd dolt push`.
- [ ] `bd doctor --check=agents` reports stale when `no-push` value changes.

---

## Summary

The architect's design is UX-correct. The key insight confirmed here: pure omission
is the right pattern for agent-consumed code blocks. The "PUSH TO REMOTE" heading
and critical rules remain accurate post-strip. No template wording changes needed
beyond the mechanical line removal.

Flagged for builder: verify the three-space indentation match in `stripDoltPushReferences`,
and add an integration test for the `bd init` + `no-push: true` path.

---

## Flow diagram

Scratch path: `/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.gc/worktrees/beads/designer/be-xj7-template.excalidraw`

PNG: `/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.gc/worktrees/beads/designer/be-xj7-template.png`

![NoPush template rendering flow](/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.gc/worktrees/beads/designer/be-xj7-template.png)
notes:
From be-j28 architecture (2026-05-27). Full implementation plan with exact code snippets on be-j28.

KEY DESIGN POINTS:
- NoPush bool defaults to false → backward compatible with existing callers
- DefaultRenderOpts() does NOT change (keeps HasRemote:true, NoPush:false)
- stripDoltPushReferences condition: if !opts.HasRemote || opts.NoPush { strip }
- Template hash changes when NoPush flips → bd doctor freshness detection works automatically
- Do NOT change dolt_autopush.go — auto-push is already opt-in (defaults off)
- Do NOT change prime.go — already reads no-push correctly for session-close protocol text
- Do NOT change internal/config/config.go or yaml_config.go — no-push is already registered

design:
# Design: `bd dolt push/pull` No-Push Guard — CLI Output and UX

**Bead:** be-di2  
**Author:** beads/designer  
**Architecture ref:** be-j28 (FR-1, FR-2, NFR-1, NFR-2)

---

## Context

When `.beads/config.yaml` sets `no-push: true`, the rig is declared local-only.
`bd dolt push` and `bd dolt pull` must exit 0 with an info message instead of
contacting any remote. Primary consumers are AI agents; secondary consumers are
human operators.

---

## Design decisions

### Q1 — Output stream: stdout or stderr?

**Decision: stdout** (as specified by architect).

Rationale:
- This is a successful no-op, not an error or warning. `stderr` semantics signal
  "something unexpected happened." A clean skip is not unexpected — it is the
  declared policy.
- AI agents (primary consumers) capture stdout as the canonical command output.
  A skip message on stderr could be silently discarded by agent harnesses that
  only read stdout.
- `fmt.Println` is consistent with other bd informational one-liners.

Risk: Scripts that pipe `bd dolt push` output will receive the message. Acceptable —
`bd dolt push` output is rarely piped, and exit 0 unambiguously signals success.

---

### Q2 — Message format

**Decision: plain text, no ANSI color or Unicode icons.**

The architect's proposed messages:
```
skipping push: rig is local-only (no-push: true)
skipping pull: rig is local-only (no-push: true)
```

These are accepted unchanged. Rationale:
- "skipping" is the canonical agent-readable signal for "action was recognized but
  intentionally not taken" — distinct from both success and failure.
- "rig is local-only" explains the WHY in human terms, not just config jargon.
- "(no-push: true)" shows the controlling config key for discoverability — an agent
  or user who wants to change behavior knows immediately where to look.
- No ANSI color: agent log aggregators often strip or misinterpret escape codes.
  The `ui` package styled output is for interactive pagers; exit messages are plain.
- No Unicode icon prefix (✓, ℹ, etc.): unnecessary chrome for a one-liner; the word
  "skipping" carries all the meaning.

---

### Q3 — `--force` flag behavior

**Decision: accept silent ignore, no message change.**

When `bd dolt push --force` is run on a no-push rig, the guard fires before `--force`
is processed. The output is identical:
```
skipping push: rig is local-only (no-push: true)
```

Alternative considered: acknowledge the flag — `"skipping push (--force ignored): ..."`.
Rejected because:
- "rig is local-only" already explains why `--force` cannot override this.
- `no-push` is a policy declaration, not a connectivity issue; `--force` addresses
  connectivity/divergence, not policy.
- Adding flag names to the message couples the message format to the flag set,
  creating maintenance burden if flags change.

---

### Q4 — Guard position

**Decision: top of `Run`, before all other logic** (NFR-2).

Must fire before `adoptGitOriginRemoteForPush` and all flag handling. This ensures:
- No network activity on no-push rigs (even failed DNS lookups).
- No side effects (no remote adoption, no config mutations).
- One guard covers the `--remote` flag path, the `--force` flag path, and the default path.

---

## Terminal mockups

### Normal push on no-push rig

```
$ bd dolt push
skipping push: rig is local-only (no-push: true)
$ echo $?
0
```

### Normal pull on no-push rig

```
$ bd dolt pull
skipping pull: rig is local-only (no-push: true)
$ echo $?
0
```

### Push with --force on no-push rig

```
$ bd dolt push --force
skipping push: rig is local-only (no-push: true)
$ echo $?
0
```

### Push with --remote on no-push rig

```
$ bd dolt push --remote=upstream
skipping push: rig is local-only (no-push: true)
$ echo $?
0
```

### Normal push on a rig WITHOUT no-push (unchanged behavior)

```
$ bd dolt push
✓ pushed to origin/main (3 commits)
$ echo $?
0
```

---

## Accessibility audit

1. **Screen readers / text-only terminals:** Plain ASCII text output, no escape codes,
   no Unicode symbols beyond parentheses. Fully accessible. ✓
2. **Log parsing / grep:** Single-line, consistent prefix — `grep "skipping push"` or
   `grep "skipping pull"` reliably catches the event. ✓
3. **Agent exit-code detection:** Exit 0 is the agent's primary signal. The message is
   secondary confirmation. No agent should fail due to this output. ✓
4. **Verbosity interaction:** No `--quiet`/`--verbose` flag interaction needed. A no-op
   command should always confirm it did not act (principle of least surprise). ✓
5. **Internationalization:** Message is English, consistent with the rest of the `bd` CLI.
   No i18n concerns at this time. ✓

---

## Summary

The architect's proposed implementation is UX-correct. No message changes recommended.
The guard position (pre-flag, pre-remote-adoption) is the right UX choice — it ensures
a clean, side-effect-free skip that agents and humans can rely on.

One implementation note for the builder: `fmt.Println` appends `\n` by default. Confirm
that no trailing whitespace is added by the surrounding log framework (if any).

---

## Flow diagram

Scratch path: `/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.gc/worktrees/beads/designer/be-di2-flow.excalidraw`

PNG: `/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.gc/worktrees/beads/designer/be-di2-flow.png`

![bd dolt push no-push guard flow](/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.gc/worktrees/beads/designer/be-di2-flow.png)

description:
# Architecture: `bd dolt push/pull` Must Respect `no-push: true`

**Bead:** be-j28  
**Date:** 2026-05-27  
**Status:** Design complete

---

## Problem Statement

When `.beads/config.yaml` declares `no-push: true`, the rig signals it is
local-only and bead-db should never be pushed to any remote. Despite this,
two things currently ignore the flag:

1. **`bd dolt push` / `bd dolt pull`** — execute unconditionally, causing
   errors when no remote is configured or when the remote is mis-aimed.
2. **BEADS INTEGRATION template** (rendered into `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
   by `bd init` / `bd setup`) — always emits `bd dolt push` in the
   Session Completion checklist, so agents that blindly run the checklist
   hit the same errors.

Both issues materialized in the 2026-05-27 gascity incident: the AGENTS.md
template told the agent to run `bd dolt push`; the Dolt remote pointed at
the public upstream; the push failed with diverged-history.

---

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| FR-1 | `bd dolt push` shall check `no-push` before contacting any remote. If true, print an INFO message to stdout and exit 0. |
| FR-2 | `bd dolt pull` shall apply the same guard, same behavior. |
| FR-3 | `bd init` and `bd setup <agent>` template renderer shall omit `bd dolt push` from Session Completion when `no-push: true`. |
| FR-4 | A rig with `no-push: true` must never cause an agent's session-completion checklist to fail on the push step. |
| FR-5 | Backward compatibility: rigs without `no-push` (or with `no-push: false`) must behave exactly as today. |

## Non-Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| NFR-1 | The `--force` flag on `bd dolt push` must also be blocked by `no-push`. |
| NFR-2 | The `no-push` guard must run before remote-adoption logic (`adoptGitOriginRemoteForPush`), so no side effects occur. |
| NFR-3 | Template hash changes when `NoPush` changes, triggering `bd doctor` staleness detection automatically. |
| NFR-4 | All callsites that construct `agents.RenderOpts` must propagate `NoPush` consistently. |

## Constraints

| Type | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| Technical | `no-push` key already exists in the config system (`v.SetDefault("no-push", false)` in `internal/config/config.go:201`) and in the YAML allowlist (`internal/config/yaml_config.go:34`). No schema changes needed. |
| Technical | `RenderOpts` is a value type with exported fields; adding `NoPush bool` is backward compatible (zero value = false = existing behavior). |
| Technical | `AgentsFileParams` (in `internal/storage/domain/beads.go`) is the DTO between the domain layer and the CLI adapter in `fs_adapters.go`. It must also grow a `NoPush bool` field to carry the signal through the use-case boundary. |
| Business | Do not change behavior for rigs where `no-push` is unset or false. |

---

## System Map (affected components)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CFG[".beads/config.yaml\nno-push: true"] --> BP["bd dolt push\ncmd/bd/dolt.go"]
    CFG --> BPL["bd dolt pull\ncmd/bd/dolt.go"]
    CFG --> DRI["detectRenderOptsImpl\ncmd/bd/setup/agents.go"]
    CFG --> INIT["bd init renderOpts\ncmd/bd/init.go:1429"]
    CFG --> PROX["init_proxied_server.go\nAgentsFileParams"]

    BP -->|"no-push=true → exit 0"| SKIP1["INFO: skipping push"]
    BPL -->|"no-push=true → exit 0"| SKIP2["INFO: skipping pull"]

    DRI --> RO["agents.RenderOpts\n{HasRemote, NoPush}"]
    INIT --> RO
    PROX --> AFP["domain.AgentsFileParams\n{HasRemote, NoPush}"]
    AFP --> FSA["fs_adapters.go\nAddAgentsInstructions"]
    FSA --> RO

    RO --> TWO["templateBodyWithOpts()\ninternal/templates/agents/render.go"]
    TWO -->|"NoPush=true → strip"| SDPR["stripDoltPushReferences()"]
    SDPR --> TMPL["Rendered AGENTS.md\n(no bd dolt push)"]
```

---

## Data Model Changes

No new tables or migrations. All changes are in-process config reads and in-memory
template rendering.

**`RenderOpts` struct** (`internal/templates/agents/render.go`):
```go
type RenderOpts struct {
    HasRemote bool  // existing: omit push when no remote configured
    NoPush    bool  // new: omit push when rig is declared local-only
}
```

**`AgentsFileParams` struct** (`internal/storage/domain/beads.go`):
```go
type AgentsFileParams struct {
    File         string
    Verbose      bool
    TemplatePath string
    Profile      string
    HasRemote    bool  // existing
    NoPush       bool  // new
}
```

---

## Use Case Flows

### UC-1: Agent runs `bd dolt push` on a no-push rig

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Agent
    participant doltPushCmd as bd dolt push
    participant Config as config.GetBool("no-push")

    Agent->>doltPushCmd: bd dolt push
    doltPushCmd->>Config: GetBool("no-push")
    Config-->>doltPushCmd: true
    doltPushCmd-->>Agent: INFO "skipping push: rig is local-only (no-push: true)"
    Note over doltPushCmd,Agent: exits 0 — checklist continues without error
```

1. Agent invokes `bd dolt push` (or `bd dolt pull`).
2. Command reads `no-push` from viper config (merged from `.beads/config.yaml`).
3. If `true`, prints `"skipping push: rig is local-only (no-push: true)"` to stdout.
4. Returns immediately with exit code 0 — the call is a no-op.
5. No remote-adoption logic, no Dolt RPC, no error.

### UC-2: `bd init` renders AGENTS.md for a no-push rig

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant User
    participant Init as bd init
    participant Config as config.GetBool
    participant Render as templateBodyWithOpts
    participant File as AGENTS.md

    User->>Init: bd init (rig has no-push: true)
    Init->>Config: GetBool("no-push")
    Config-->>Init: true
    Init->>Render: RenderSectionWithOpts(profile, {HasRemote:…, NoPush:true})
    Render->>Render: stripDoltPushReferences(body)
    Render-->>Init: template body without "bd dolt push"
    Init->>File: write rendered AGENTS.md
    File-->>User: Session Completion has no dolt push step
```

1. `bd init` constructs `agents.RenderOpts` with `NoPush: config.GetBool("no-push")`.
2. `RenderSectionWithOpts` calls `templateBodyWithOpts(profile, opts)`.
3. `templateBodyWithOpts` calls `stripDoltPushReferences(body)` when `opts.NoPush` is true.
4. The three-space-indented `   bd dolt push\n` line is removed from the Session Completion code block.
5. Rendered section is written to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`.
6. Template hash changes (because body changed), so `bd doctor` will flag stale sections on rigs that already have the old template — correct behavior.

### UC-3: `bd setup claude` updates existing AGENTS.md

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant User
    participant Setup as bd setup claude
    participant DRI as detectRenderOptsImpl
    participant Render as RenderSectionWithOpts
    participant File as AGENTS.md

    User->>Setup: bd setup claude
    Setup->>DRI: detectRenderOpts()
    DRI->>DRI: config.GetBool("no-push") → true
    DRI-->>Setup: RenderOpts{HasRemote:…, NoPush:true}
    Setup->>Render: RenderSectionWithOpts(profile, opts)
    Render-->>Setup: body without bd dolt push
    Setup->>File: replace beads section
```

1. `detectRenderOptsImpl` reads both `sync.remote` / `sync.git-remote` and `no-push`.
2. Returns `RenderOpts{..., NoPush: true}`.
3. Rendered section omits `bd dolt push`.

---

## Implementation Plan (for builder)

### Change 1: Guard `bd dolt push` and `bd dolt pull` (`cmd/bd/dolt.go`)

At the **top** of `doltPushCmd.Run` (before any other logic, including `adoptGitOriginRemoteForPush`):

```go
if config.GetBool("no-push") {
    fmt.Println("skipping push: rig is local-only (no-push: true)")
    return
}
```

Same at the top of `doltPullCmd.Run`:

```go
if config.GetBool("no-push") {
    fmt.Println("skipping pull: rig is local-only (no-push: true)")
    return
}
```

Both the named-remote code path (`--remote` flag) and the default path must be guarded. Since the guard fires before any branching in the Run function, a single check at entry covers all paths.

`maybeAutoPush` in `dolt_autopush.go` is **not** affected: `isDoltAutoPushEnabled` returns `false` by default (opt-in via `dolt.auto-push=true`), so a no-push rig that never set `dolt.auto-push` already silently skips auto-push. No change needed there.

### Change 2: Add `NoPush` to `RenderOpts` (`internal/templates/agents/render.go`)

```go
type RenderOpts struct {
    HasRemote bool
    NoPush    bool  // when true, omit bd dolt push from session completion
}
```

In `templateBodyWithOpts`:

```go
if !opts.HasRemote || opts.NoPush {
    body = stripDoltPushReferences(body)
}
```

`DefaultRenderOpts()` stays as `RenderOpts{HasRemote: true}` — `NoPush` defaults to `false`, which is backward compatible.

### Change 3: Populate `NoPush` in `detectRenderOptsImpl` (`cmd/bd/setup/agents.go`)

```go
var detectRenderOptsImpl = func() agents.RenderOpts {
    return agents.RenderOpts{
        HasRemote: config.GetString("sync.remote") != "" || config.GetString("sync.git-remote") != "",
        NoPush:    config.GetBool("no-push"),
    }
}
```

### Change 4: Populate `NoPush` in `bd init` (`cmd/bd/init.go:1429`)

```go
renderOpts := agents.RenderOpts{
    HasRemote: shouldWireInitRemote(syncURL, syncFromRemote, syncURLFromConfig, syncURLFromGitOrigin),
    NoPush:    config.GetBool("no-push"),
}
```

### Change 5: Add `NoPush` to `AgentsFileParams` domain DTO (`internal/storage/domain/beads.go`)

```go
type AgentsFileParams struct {
    File         string
    Verbose      bool
    TemplatePath string
    Profile      string
    HasRemote    bool
    NoPush       bool  // new
}
```

### Change 6: Propagate `NoPush` in `fs_adapters.go`

```go
AddAgentsInstructions: func(p domain.AgentsFileParams) {
    addAgentsInstructions(p.File, p.Verbose, p.TemplatePath, agents.Profile(p.Profile),
        agents.RenderOpts{HasRemote: p.HasRemote, NoPush: p.NoPush})
},
```

### Change 7: Populate `NoPush` in `init_proxied_server.go`

```go
_ = t.fsUseCase.AddAgentsInstructions(ctx, domain.AgentsFileParams{
    File:         resolvedAgentsFile,
    Verbose:      !in.quiet,
    TemplatePath: agentsTemplate,
    Profile:      agentsProfileStr,
    HasRemote:    t.remoteURL != "",
    NoPush:       config.GetBool("no-push"),
})
```

---

## Affected Files Summary

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `cmd/bd/dolt.go` | Guard `doltPushCmd.Run` and `doltPullCmd.Run` with `no-push` check |
| `internal/templates/agents/render.go` | Add `NoPush bool` to `RenderOpts`; apply strip when `NoPush=true` |
| `cmd/bd/setup/agents.go` | Populate `NoPush` in `detectRenderOptsImpl` |
| `cmd/bd/init.go` | Populate `NoPush` in `renderOpts` at line 1429 |
| `internal/storage/domain/beads.go` | Add `NoPush bool` to `AgentsFileParams` |
| `cmd/bd/fs_adapters.go` | Pass `NoPush: p.NoPush` through to `RenderOpts` |
| `cmd/bd/init_proxied_server.go` | Populate `NoPush` in `AgentsFileParams` literal |

Files **not** changed:
- `cmd/bd/dolt_autopush.go` — auto-push is opt-in and already skips by default
- `cmd/bd/prime.go` — already correctly reads `no-push` for session close protocol text
- `internal/config/config.go` — `no-push` default is already set
- `internal/config/yaml_config.go` — `no-push` already in YAML allowlist

---

## Security Controls

No trust-boundary changes. All inputs are local config reads. No network calls
are added; the change prevents network calls.

---

## Risks

| Likelihood | Impact | Risk | Mitigation |
|-----------|--------|------|-----------|
| Low | Medium | Existing rigs have stale AGENTS.md with `bd dolt push` after this fix ships | Existing `bd doctor` freshness check (`--check=agents`) will flag stale sections; agents are already trained to re-run `bd init` on staleness |
| Low | Low | `AgentsFileParams.NoPush` not populated in some edge-case callsite | Only 1 external callsite (`init_proxied_server.go`); covered by Change 7 above |
| Low | Low | `NoPush=true` + `HasRemote=true` combination: strip is applied but remote is actually configured | Correct — if operator declared `no-push: true`, push should be skipped regardless of whether a remote exists |

---

## Trade-offs & Alternatives Considered

**Alt A: Reuse `HasRemote=false` to mean "no-push" in the template**  
Rejected. `HasRemote=false` means "no remote configured — go set one up". `no-push=true`
means "a remote may exist, but this rig intentionally doesn't use it". Conflating them
gives wrong guidance in the rendered template ("set up a remote" vs. "intentionally
skipped"). Distinct fields preserve distinct semantics.

**Alt B: Add a `--no-push` flag to `bd dolt push` instead of reading config**  
Rejected. The config-based approach is declarative — the rig declares its policy once.
A flag requires every caller (including auto-generated AGENTS.md) to remember to pass it.

**Alt C: Replace `bd dolt push` with a commented-out line in the template**  
Considered. "omit OR render as no-op comment" is in the bead's acceptance criteria.
Pure omission is simpler and cleaner; a commented-out command could confuse agents
into trying to un-comment it. `bd prime` already explains the session close protocol
correctly for `no-push=true` rigs. Omit wins.

**Alt D: Guard auto-push (`maybeAutoPush`) with `no-push` too**  
Not needed. `dolt.auto-push` defaults to `false` (opt-in). A `no-push` rig that never
set `dolt.auto-push=true` already has auto-push disabled. Adding a redundant guard
would be defensive noise.

title: [upstream] schema loader: panic on duplicate migration versions (close systemic dup-collision class)
description:
Upstream contribution to gastownhall/beads. Add a duplicate-version guard to the migration loader so the SAME class of bug that has now bitten us TWICE is caught at build time forever.

## Why this exists

Sequential integer migration versions collide whenever two long-lived branches both claim 'the next number' and one merges first. The loader has no duplicate detection and silently under-applies the second migration.

Two empirical incidents:
- **0033 collision (2026-05-16)** — broke CI Test (Embedded Dolt Storage). Manually renumbered to 0043 to resolve. PR thread captures the diagnosis.
- **0043 collision (2026-05-27, our PR #3663)** — same shape. Renumbered to 0048 today (commits 5a94c1ffb + a36aa38c5 on release/be-1n9-pq5-purge). Would have re-broken CI at merge if not caught by investigator audit.

Investigator (be-36t, 2026-05-27) flagged the systemic root cause and recommended a small upstream contribution.

## Root cause (file:line)

`internal/storage/schema/schema.go`:
- L527 `list()` enumerates migration files via embedded FS.
- L110 `parseVersion()` extracts the integer prefix from each filename.
- L543 `sort.Slice` sorts the migrations by version — **NOT stable**, so two files at the same version come out in non-deterministic order.
- L658-672 apply loop gates on `mf.version <= current`; L670 records via `INSERT IGNORE ... VALUES(version)`. The IGNORE means a duplicate version is silently dropped from the migrations table; only one of the two files gets recorded.

Net effect: two files at version N → unstable order picks one to apply 'first' → only that one gets recorded → the other appears applied (no replay) but its schema deltas are missing. Tests that exercise the not-applied migration's behavior fail nondeterministically.

## Proposed fix

Two layers, either independently sufficient; both is best.

### Layer 1 — runtime guard in list() (~10-15 LOC)

After parseVersion across all files, walk the parsed versions and panic on the first duplicate. Symmetric with the existing 'panic on bad filename' at L539:

```go
seen := make(map[int]string, len(migrations))
for _, m := range migrations {
    if prior, ok := seen[m.version]; ok {
        panic(fmt.Sprintf(
            "duplicate migration version %d: %q and %q — renumber one before commit",
            m.version, prior, m.filename,
        ))
    }
    seen[m.version] = m.filename
}
```

Fail-fast at process start instead of nondeterministic test failure days later.

### Layer 2 — CI check (~10 LOC of shell or a tiny Go tool)

Cheap to add to .github/workflows: glob `internal/storage/schema/migrations/*.up.sql`, extract numeric prefix, check for duplicates, exit non-zero with a clear message. Catches the collision at PR-CI time, before any test even compiles.

Either layer would have caught both 0033 and 0043 at the moment of merge instead of after the fact via a storage test that nobody traces back to migration ordering.

## Done-when

- [ ] schema.go list() panics on duplicate version with a useful message naming both files
- [ ] Unit test asserts the panic message format (so the contract is locked)
- [ ] (Optional, recommended) CI workflow step that pre-checks migration uniqueness with no Go build needed
- [ ] PR opened against gastownhall/beads main with the above
- [ ] CI passes on the PR

## Not in scope

- The DROP-stale-DB and date-index work currently on `release/be-1n9-pq5-purge` (PR #3663) — that's a separate PR
- Any refactor of the broader migration loader (sort stability, stronger filename schema, etc.) — narrower the scope, faster the merge

## Maintainer-engagement expectations

We are NOT maintainers of `gastownhall/beads` and have no merge authority. Per operator standing-order, we contribute the best we can and don't expect maintainer attention — this PR joins our existing backlog. The work earns its keep regardless of upstream merge timing: even if it sits, the next contributor who hits a third version collision will find the diagnosis here.

Source bead: be-36t (PR #3663 investigator triage, gm-wisp-x440sp).
notes:
Implementation plan:
1. Add checkNoDuplicateVersions([]migrationFile) helper in schema.go — panics on dup naming both files
2. Call in list() after collection, before sort.Slice
3. Unit test asserting panic message format
4. CI shell step in ci.yml to catch dups at PR time (no Go build needed)

title: Decision: PR #4013 archive-default conflicts with main opt-in policy
description:
Investigator handoff from be-vun (PR #4013, fork branch feat/be-6lydih-be-tsjke3-archive-alias).
PR is OURS (author quad341). External reviewer: maphew (awaiting response). Rebase onto current
main (cee594143) is CLEAN. CI red = 4 cmd/bd tests; ALL pass on clean main, fail on the branch
(quad341's "pre-existing/unrelated" claim DISPROVEN by running them on origin/main).

## DECISION NEEDED (product policy — above investigator seat)
PR #4013 makes archive ON by default for Dolt: bd init writes archive.format=jsonl
(internal/config/config.go ArchiveDefaultForBackend dolt->jsonl; cmd/bd/init.go ~L1310). Since
export.auto is aliased to archive.format, this REVERSES main's opt-in policy (auto-export OFF by
default), enforced by cmd/bd TestInitNonInteractiveAutoExportDefaultOffAndOptIn.
  Option A (RECOMMENDED): conform to opt-in — ArchiveDefaultForBackend returns "none" (or init
    does not enable); archive.* schema + doctor status + size fix still ship, just opt-in.
  Option B: keep on-by-default — also requires reversing main's opt-in policy + test (product call).
  Option C: close PR (feature not wanted; source beads be-6lydih/be-tsjke3/be-qqggak all deleted).

## Mechanical bugs to fix REGARDLESS of A/B (maphew review, now proven)
F1 (proven by 3 failing tests): export.auto<->archive.format alias is HALF-WIRED. bd config
  get/set export.auto route through archive.format (cmd/bd/config.go configSet ~L143 / configGet
  ~L248) but the runtime exporter cmd/bd/export_auto.go:49 still gates on the RAW export.auto key
  and uses export.path/export.interval. Net: enabling via the alias never turns the runtime on;
  archive.path/archive.throttle_seconds are ignored by the exporter. Fix: route maybeAutoExport +
  path/throttle resolution through the archive alias with legacy fallback.
F2 (maphew): internal/config/alias.go ResolveArchiveFormat drops GetArchiveFormat's validation
  error (no early-return on err) -> bogus archive.format silently falls back to none/alias;
  cmd/bd/doctor/archive.go CheckArchiveConfig (L24-59) treats any non-none as healthy. Fix:
  surface invalid archive.format as a doctor failure; do not swallow the error.

## Done-when
- [ ] cmd/bd TestInitNonInteractiveAutoExportDefaultOffAndOptIn passes (gated by A/B)
- [ ] cmd/bd TestAutoExportGitAddFailureExitsNonZero / SkipsEmptyExportOverPopulatedJSONL /
      SkipsWhenExistingJSONLHasIDsMissingFromStore pass
- [ ] new test: bd config set archive.path X honored by exporter (F1)
- [ ] new test: bogus archive.format reported as doctor failure (F2)
- [ ] reply to maphew on PR #4013 enumerating each point + commit

## Status / repro
Clean rebase reproducible: git worktree add -b X <tmp> <PR-head>; git rebase origin/main (no conflicts).
NOT pushed (would re-trigger red CI without the decision). PR left as-is pending this decision.
close_reason: Option C — PR #4013 closed. Reasoning: scope creep (doctor path fix grew to include new archive.* schema + alias + default-flip for Dolt). Default-flip reverses main's opt-in policy and deserves its own PR with explicit framing. F1/F2 mechanical bugs acknowledged to maphew but not addressed in this PR; can come back as a narrow follow-up if wanted.

title: perf(dolt): auto-skip wisps merge when wisps table empty (server DoltStore)
description:
Salvaged from PR #4021 (feat/be-perf-q1-q2-q3-q5-spike), closed as superseded by investigator.

CONTEXT
The PR's stated work (Q1+Q2+Q3+Q5; beads bd-xoi0x/bd-qi4qr/bd-co6m6/bd-wsgws)
all landed on main via a cleaner shared-issueops refactor:
  - bd13f473c perf(count): Q1 SQL COUNT(*) aggregate
  - 9a29a158f perf(search): Q2+Q3+Q5 skip-wisps merge, id-shrunk Pattern B, wisp count cache
  - c1091b804 test(spike): joinIter panic repro

THE ONE THING NOT ON MAIN
The server DoltStore (internal/storage/dolt/) in that PR auto-enables
filter.SkipWisps when the wisps table is empty, via a per-process cache
(isWispTableEmpty / invalidateWispCountCache, wired into 6 write sites).
main's Q5 only skips wisps when the CALLER sets SkipWisps
(issueops/search.go:37, count.go:28) — it does NOT auto-skip on an empty
wisps table. So an empty-wisps repo still pays the merge unless callers opt in.

IF PURSUED (triage decision — may not be worth it)
- Implement cleanly on a fresh branch; do NOT revive the spike.
- Do NOT port the spike's dead code: dolt/queries.go getChildrenWithParents
  and getDescendantIDs (no callers), and the half-finished blocked-IDs cache
  (fields declared+cleared, never populated/read).
- Add a benchmark proving the empty-wisps fast path before/after.
- Consider doing it in the shared issueops layer so both backends benefit,
  not just the server DoltStore.

This is unrouted on purpose: it is a minor optimization and main already has
the caller-opt-in skip. Triage before building.

title: [BLOCKED on #4021 close] Follow-up to superseded spike PR #4021: bd query SkipWisps + server-mode wisp-cache coherence
description:
Context: PR #4021 (branch feat/be-perf-q1-q2-q3-q5-spike) is a superseded perf
spike. Its four headline optimizations' SAFE parts already landed on main via
focused PRs: Q1 SQL COUNT(*) = bd13f473c; Q2 SkipWisps flag + count/list callers
and Q3 Pattern B = 9a29a158f; spike test = c1091b804. Investigator recommended
closing #4021 as superseded (see be-20g). This bead tracks the bits that do NOT
yet exist on main, so they are not lost when #4021 closes.

[BLOCKED on mayor's decision to close #4021 — do not action until then.]

1. bd query SkipWisps  (SAFE, trivial re-land)
   cmd/bd/query.go sets searchFilter.SkipWisps = true. Main's `bd query` does NOT
   set it, though `bd list` and `bd count` do (landed via 9a29a158f). This is an
   explicit caller opt-in ("bd query never needs ephemeral wisps") and is always
   correct regardless of table state. If wanted, re-land as a one-line focused PR.
   Confirm the product intent that `bd query` should exclude wisps (consistent
   with list/count).

2. Server-mode DoltStore wisp-empty auto-cache  (NEEDS DESIGN — do NOT port as-is)
   The spike adds a per-process "wisps table empty" cache to internal/storage/dolt
   (isWispTableEmpty / wispCountCached / wispCountZero in dolt/queries.go and
   dolt/store.go; invalidations in dolt/issues.go and dolt/ephemeral_routing.go)
   that auto-sets SkipWisps when the table is believed empty. This NEVER landed on
   main: 9a29a158f's commit MESSAGE claims "per-process wisp row-count cache on
   DoltStore" but its actual diff only added the SkipWisps FLAG (issueops/search.go,
   issueops/count.go, types.go, cmd/bd callers) — not the auto-cache. The auto-cache
   is sound for the single-writer EMBEDDED backend, but DoltStore is the SERVER-mode
   / shared-dolt backend used for CONCURRENT multi-writer access (store_factory:
   newDoltStore -> dolt.New when ServerMode; usesSQLServer()/IsSharedServerMode).
   Invalidation is in-process only, so process A's "table empty" belief is not
   invalidated when process B inserts the first wisp -> stale auto-skip -> A's
   searches silently omit wisps. If a server-mode wisp-empty optimization is wanted,
   it needs a cross-process invalidation strategy (or a short TTL), not the spike's
   per-process cache. Not yet proven as a runtime bug (no repro); flagged as a
   correctness RISK to evaluate before any port.

Out of scope: do NOT salvage PR #4021's branch directly — it is a messy rebased
spike whose sole CI break is a duplicate CountIssuesByGroup in
embeddeddolt/list_queries.go (main already has it in embeddeddolt/counts.go).

title: Fix stripDoltPushReferences to use exact-line match instead of substring
description:
internal/templates/agents/render.go: stripDoltPushReferences uses strings.ReplaceAll(body, '   bd dolt push\n', '') which matches the 3-space pattern as a SUBSTRING. A 4-space-indented line '    bd dolt push\n' is incorrectly stripped to ' ' instead of being left unchanged.

This is a pre-existing bug (predates commit efad1869d). Does not affect real-world output today because no template content contains a 4-space-indented 'bd dolt push' line. Exposed by validator's TestStripDoltPushReferences_NonMatchingIndents test.

Fix: change the replacement to anchor the match at start-of-line, e.g.:
  body = strings.ReplaceAll(body, "\n   bd dolt push\n", "\n")
or handle the BOF case too. A regex with (?m)^   bd dolt push$ would be cleaner but strings package doesn't support it — use regexp.MustCompile if needed.
notes: Discovered during review of be-85s (efad1869d). Not a blocker for that PR — filed separately per review protocol.
close_reason: Fix applied via rebase of feat/be-3w6-be-0c8-nopush-dolt: commit 0541f7597 anchors stripDoltPushReferences with newline padding. Also resolved init.go merge conflict (combined isDoltLocalOnly()+NoPush).
